verses.kjv: And Zedekiah the king said unto Jeremiah, I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they mock me.
verses.decoded: King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have surrendered to the Babylonians; I worry they will hand me over to them and make fun of me."

verses.kjv: But Jeremiah said, They shall not deliver thee. Obey, I beseech thee, the voice of the LORD, which I speak unto thee: so it shall be well unto thee, and thy soul shall live.
verses.decoded: Jeremiah replied, "They will not hand you over. Please obey the LORD's command that I am telling you, and things will go well for you and you will live."

verses.kjv: But if thou refuse to go forth, this is the word that the LORD hath shewed me:
verses.decoded: But if you refuse to go, this is the message the LORD has shown me:

verses.kjv: And, behold, all the women that are left in the king of Judah’s house shall be brought forth to the king of Babylon’s princes, and those women shall say, Thy friends have set thee on, and have prevailed against thee: thy feet are sunk in the mire, and they are turned away back.
verses.decoded: All the women left in the king of Judah’s palace will be taken to the Babylonian officials, and they will say, 'Your own friends have tricked you and defeated you; you are stuck in the mud and have turned back.'

verses.kjv: So they shall bring out all thy wives and thy children to the Chaldeans: and thou shalt not escape out of their hand, but shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon: and thou shalt cause this city to be burned with fire.
verses.decoded: They will take all your wives and children to the Babylonians, and you will not escape their control. You will be captured by the king of Babylon and will see the city burned by fire.

verses.kjv: Then said Zedekiah unto Jeremiah, Let no man know of these words, and thou shalt not die.
verses.decoded: Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Don’t let anyone hear these words, and you will not be killed."

verses.kjv: But if the princes hear that I have talked with thee, and they come unto thee, and say unto thee, Declare unto us now what thou hast said unto the king, hide it not from us, and we will not put thee to death; also what the king said unto thee:
verses.decoded: But if the officials find out I spoke with you and ask you to tell them what you said to the king, promising not to kill you, and also what the king said to you,

verses.kjv: Then thou shalt say unto them, I presented my supplication before the king, that he would not cause me to return to Jonathan’s house, to die there.
verses.decoded: Then you should tell them, 'I asked the king not to send me back to Jonathan’s house to die there.'

verses.kjv: Then came all the princes unto Jeremiah, and asked him: and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they left off speaking with him; for the matter was not perceived.
verses.decoded: All the officials came to Jeremiah and asked him, and he told them exactly what the king had told him. So they stopped questioning him because they didn’t suspect anything.

verses.kjv: So Jeremiah abode in the court of the prison until the day that Jerusalem was taken: and he was there when Jerusalem was taken.
verses.decoded: Jeremiah stayed in the prison courtyard until Jerusalem was captured, and he was there when it happened.

verses.kjv: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it.
verses.decoded: In the ninth year of King Zedekiah of Judah, during the tenth month, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and his entire army came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.

verses.kjv: And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, the city was broken up.
verses.decoded: In the eleventh year of King Zedekiah, on the ninth day of the fourth month, the city was breached.

verses.kjv: And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in, and sat in the middle gate, even Nergalsharezer, Samgarnebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, with all the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon.
verses.decoded: All the Babylonian officials entered and sat at the middle gate, including Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Rabmag, and all the other Babylonian princes.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night, by the way of the king’s garden, by the gate betwixt the two walls: and he went out the way of the plain.
verses.decoded: When King Zedekiah of Judah saw the Babylonian officials and soldiers, he and his men fled the city at night through the king’s garden, exiting by the gate between the two walls, and escaped toward the plains.

verses.kjv: But the Chaldeans’ army pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he gave judgment upon him.
verses.decoded: But the Babylonian army chased after them and caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They took him to King Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah in Hamath, where the king passed judgment on him.

verses.kjv: Then the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes: also the king of Babylon slew all the nobles of Judah.
verses.decoded: At Riblah, the Babylonian king killed Zedekiah’s sons in front of him and also executed all the nobles of Judah.

verses.kjv: Moreover he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, and bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon.
verses.decoded: Then the king blinded Zedekiah, chained him, and took him to Babylon as a prisoner.

verses.kjv: And the Chaldeans burned the king’s house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: The Babylonians burned the king’s palace and the houses of the people, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive into Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to him, with the rest of the people that remained.
verses.decoded: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took the remaining people in the city captive and brought them to Babylon, including those who had surrendered and the rest who were left.

verses.kjv: But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left of the poor of the people, which had nothing, in the land of Judah, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
verses.decoded: However, Nebuzaradan left some poor people who owned nothing in the land of Judah and gave them vineyards and fields to live on.

verses.kjv: Now Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, saying,
verses.decoded: King Nebuchadnezzar gave orders to Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, about the prophet Jeremiah, saying,

verses.kjv: Take him, and look well to him, and do him no harm; but do unto him even as he shall say unto thee.
verses.decoded: Take care of him and do not harm him; treat him exactly as he instructs you.

verses.kjv: So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard sent, and Nebushasban, Rabsaris, and Nergalsharezer, Rabmag, and all the king of Babylon’s princes;
verses.decoded: Nebuzaradan sent orders to Nebushasban, Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer, Rabmag, and all the Babylonian officials.

verses.kjv: Even they sent, and took Jeremiah out of the court of the prison, and committed him unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, that he should carry him home: so he dwelt among the people.
verses.decoded: They took Jeremiah out of prison and handed him over to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, so he could live among the people.

verses.kjv: Now the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the prison, saying,
verses.decoded: While Jeremiah was still confined in the prison courtyard, the LORD spoke to him, saying,

verses.kjv: Go and speak to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, saying, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil, and not for good; and they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.
verses.decoded: Go and tell Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, 'This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring my judgment on this city for disaster, not for good, and it will happen soon, right before your eyes.'

verses.kjv: But I will deliver thee in that day, saith the LORD: and thou shalt not be given into the hand of the men of whom thou art afraid.
verses.decoded: But I will rescue you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be handed over to the people you fear.

verses.kjv: For I will surely deliver thee, and thou shalt not fall by the sword, but thy life shall be for a prey unto thee: because thou hast put thy trust in me, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: I will definitely save you; you will not be killed by the sword, and your life will be your reward because you have trusted in me, declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all that were carried away captive of Jerusalem and Judah, which were carried away captive unto Babylon.
verses.decoded: After Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, released Jeremiah at Ramah—where he had been taken captive in chains along with the others from Jerusalem and Judah who were exiled to Babylon—the LORD spoke to Jeremiah.

verses.kjv: And the captain of the guard took Jeremiah, and said unto him, The LORD thy God hath pronounced this evil upon this place.
verses.decoded: The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and told him, 'The LORD your God has declared disaster against this land.'

verses.kjv: Now the LORD hath brought it, and done according as he hath said: because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed his voice, therefore this thing is come upon you.
verses.decoded: Now the LORD has brought this disaster and fulfilled what He said, because you have sinned against Him and refused to obey His commands. That is why this has happened to you.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which were upon thine hand. If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon, come; and I will look well unto thee: but if it seem ill unto thee to come with me into Babylon, forbear: behold, all the land is before thee: whither it seemeth good and convenient for thee to go, thither go.
verses.decoded: Today I am freeing you from the chains on your hands. If you want to come with me to Babylon, you may, and I will take good care of you. But if you don’t want to go, that’s fine too. The whole land is open to you—go wherever you think is best.

verses.kjv: Now while he was not yet gone back, he said, Go back also to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon hath made governor over the cities of Judah, and dwell with him among the people: or go wheresoever it seemeth convenient unto thee to go. So the captain of the guard gave him victuals and a reward, and let him go.
verses.decoded: Before I leave, go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed governor over Judah’s cities. Live with him among the people, or go wherever you find suitable. The captain of the guard gave Jeremiah food and a reward, and then let him go.

verses.kjv: Then went Jeremiah unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and dwelt with him among the people that were left in the land.
verses.decoded: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived there among the people remaining in the land.

verses.kjv: Now when all the captains of the forces which were in the fields, even they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed unto him men, and women, and children, and of the poor of the land, of them that were not carried away captive to Babylon;
verses.decoded: When all the military commanders and their soldiers in the fields heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam as governor over the land, and had given him responsibility for the men, women, children, and poor people who were not taken captive to Babylon,

verses.kjv: Then they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
verses.decoded: They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, including Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of a Maachathite, along with their men.

verses.kjv: And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan sware unto them and to their men, saying, Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.
verses.decoded: Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore to them and their men, 'Don’t be afraid to serve the Babylonians. Live in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.'

verses.kjv: As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah, to serve the Chaldeans, which will come unto us: but ye, gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that ye have taken.
verses.decoded: As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to serve the Babylonians when they arrive. But you, gather wine, summer fruits, and oil, store them in your containers, and live in the cities you have captured.

verses.kjv: Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan;
verses.decoded: When all the Jews living in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other countries heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah and appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan to govern them,

verses.kjv: Even all the Jews returned out of all places whither they were driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, unto Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruits very much.
verses.decoded: All the Jews returned from the places where they had been scattered and came back to Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they gathered large amounts of wine and summer fruits.

verses.kjv: Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields, came to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
verses.decoded: Johanan son of Kareah and all the military commanders in the fields also came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,

verses.kjv: And said unto him, Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites hath sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee? But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not.
verses.decoded: and told him, 'Are you sure that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?' But Gedaliah did not believe them.

verses.kjv: Then Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?
verses.decoded: Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, 'Please let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he kill you and cause all the Jews gathered around you to scatter and the remaining people in Judah to be destroyed?'

verses.kjv: But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.
verses.decoded: But Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, said to Johanan, son of Kareah, 'You must not do this because you are lying about Ishmael.'

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and the princes of the king, even ten men with him, came unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah.
verses.decoded: In the seventh month, Ishmael, son of Nethaniah and descendant of the royal family, came to Mizpah with ten men, including some of the king's officials. They ate together with Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, in Mizpah.

verses.kjv: Then arose Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men that were with him, and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
verses.decoded: Then Ishmael and the ten men with him got up and killed Gedaliah, who had been appointed governor of the land by the king of Babylon.

verses.kjv: Ishmael also slew all the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war.
verses.decoded: Ishmael also killed all the Jews who were with Gedaliah in Mizpah, as well as the Chaldeans and soldiers present there.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass the second day after he had slain Gedaliah, and no man knew it,
verses.decoded: On the second day after killing Gedaliah, no one knew what had happened.

verses.kjv: That there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the LORD.
verses.decoded: Eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They had shaved their beards, torn their clothes, and made cuts on themselves. They carried offerings and incense to bring to the house of the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.
verses.decoded: Ishmael left Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he met them, he said, 'Come to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam.'

verses.kjv: And it was so, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him.
verses.decoded: When they entered the city, Ishmael and his men killed them and threw their bodies into a pit.

verses.kjv: But ten men were found among them that said unto Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he forbare, and slew them not among their brethren.
verses.decoded: Ten men among them begged Ishmael not to kill them because they had stored wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the fields. So Ishmael spared them and did not kill them with the others.

verses.kjv: Now the pit wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain.
verses.decoded: The pit where Ishmael threw the bodies was originally dug by King Asa to defend against Baasha, king of Israel. Ishmael filled this pit with the men he had killed because of Gedaliah.

verses.kjv: Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king’s daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites.
verses.decoded: Ishmael took captive all the remaining people in Mizpah, including the king's daughters and others Nebuzaradan had entrusted to Gedaliah. Then Ishmael left to go to the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
verses.decoded: When Johanan, son of Kareah, and all the military leaders with him heard about the terrible things Ishmael had done,

verses.kjv: Then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great waters that are in Gibeon.
verses.decoded: They gathered all their men and went to fight Ishmael. They found him near the large waters in Gibeon.

verses.kjv: Now it came to pass, that when all the people which were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad.
verses.decoded: When the people with Ishmael saw Johanan and his commanders, they were happy.

verses.kjv: So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah cast about and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah.
verses.decoded: All the captives Ishmael had taken from Mizpah turned back and went to Johanan, son of Kareah.

verses.kjv: But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites.
verses.decoded: Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and fled to the Ammonites.

verses.kjv: Then took Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after that he had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, even mighty men of war, and the women, and the children, and the eunuchs, whom he had brought again from Gibeon:
verses.decoded: Then Johanan son of Kareah, along with all the military leaders with him, took all the remaining people he had rescued from Ishmael son of Nethaniah at Mizpah after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. This included strong warriors, women, children, and eunuchs whom Johanan had brought back from Gibeon.

verses.kjv: And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
verses.decoded: They left and stayed at Chimham, a place near Bethlehem, intending to travel into Egypt.

verses.kjv: Because of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land.
verses.decoded: They were afraid of the Babylonians (Chaldeans) because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, who had been appointed governor of the land by the king of Babylon.

verses.kjv: Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest, came near,
verses.decoded: Then all the military commanders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least important to the most important, came close.

verses.kjv: And said unto Jeremiah the prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us unto the LORD thy God, even for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes do behold us:)
verses.decoded: They said to Jeremiah the prophet, 'Please accept our request and pray to the LORD your God for all of us survivors; we are only a small remnant compared to before, as you can see.'

verses.kjv: That the LORD thy God may shew us the way wherein we may walk, and the thing that we may do.
verses.decoded: So that the LORD your God will show us the way to live and what we should do.

verses.kjv: Then Jeremiah the prophet said unto them, I have heard you; behold, I will pray unto the LORD your God according to your words; and it shall come to pass, that whatsoever thing the LORD shall answer you, I will declare it unto you; I will keep nothing back from you.
verses.decoded: Jeremiah replied, 'I have heard you. I will pray to the LORD your God as you asked, and whatever answer the LORD gives, I will tell you everything. I will not hide anything from you.'

verses.kjv: Then they said to Jeremiah, The LORD be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not even according to all things for the which the LORD thy God shall send thee to us.
verses.decoded: They said to Jeremiah, 'May the LORD be a true and faithful witness between us if we do not obey everything the LORD your God tells you to say to us.'

verses.kjv: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
verses.decoded: Whether the message is good or bad, we will obey the LORD our God, to whom we have sent you, so that things will go well for us when we obey Him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah.
verses.decoded: After ten days, the LORD gave Jeremiah a message.

verses.kjv: Then called he Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces which were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
verses.decoded: Jeremiah called Johanan son of Kareah, all the military commanders with him, and all the people, from the least important to the most important,

verses.kjv: And said unto them, Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, unto whom ye sent me to present your supplication before him;
verses.decoded: and said to them, 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says—the one you sent me to pray to on your behalf:'

verses.kjv: If ye will still abide in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up: for I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you.
verses.decoded: If you stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, because I regret the harm I caused you.

verses.kjv: Be not afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom ye are afraid; be not afraid of him, saith the LORD: for I am with you to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.
verses.decoded: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not be afraid, says the LORD, because I am with you to save you and rescue you from his power.

verses.kjv: And I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you, and cause you to return to your own land.
verses.decoded: I will show you kindness so that the king of Babylon will also show you mercy and allow you to return to your own land.

verses.kjv: But if ye say, We will not dwell in this land, neither obey the voice of the LORD your God,
verses.decoded: But if you say, 'We will not live in this land or obey the LORD your God,'

verses.kjv: Saying, No; but we will go into the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor have hunger of bread; and there will we dwell:
verses.decoded: saying, 'No, we will go to Egypt, where there is no war, no sound of battle, and no hunger; we will live there,'

verses.kjv: And now therefore hear the word of the LORD, ye remnant of Judah; Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; If ye wholly set your faces to enter into Egypt, and go to sojourn there;
verses.decoded: Now listen to the word of the LORD, you survivors of Judah: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says—if you decide to go to Egypt and live there temporarily,

verses.kjv: Then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine, whereof ye were afraid, shall follow close after you there in Egypt; and there ye shall die.
verses.decoded: What you feared—the sword—will catch up with you in Egypt, and the famine you were afraid of will follow you there. You will die in Egypt.

verses.kjv: So shall it be with all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there; they shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence: and none of them shall remain or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them.
verses.decoded: All those who decide to go to Egypt to live there will die by the sword, famine, and disease. None will survive or escape the disaster I will bring.

verses.kjv: For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured forth upon you, when ye shall enter into Egypt: and ye shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach; and ye shall see this place no more.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and fury have been poured out on Jerusalem’s people, so will my fury be poured out on you when you enter Egypt. You will become a curse, a horror, a disgrace, and a shame, and you will never see this land again.

verses.kjv: The LORD hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day.
verses.decoded: The LORD says to you, the remaining people of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Be sure that I have warned you today.

verses.kjv: For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us unto the LORD our God; and according unto all that the LORD our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it.
verses.decoded: But you were dishonest in your hearts when you sent me to ask the LORD your God to pray for you, saying, ‘Tell us whatever the LORD our God says, and we will do it.’

verses.kjv: And now I have this day declared it to you; but ye have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God, nor any thing for the which he hath sent me unto you.
verses.decoded: Today I have told you what the LORD said, but you have not obeyed the LORD your God or anything I was sent to tell you.

verses.kjv: Now therefore know certainly that ye shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place whither ye desire to go and to sojourn.
verses.decoded: So now be sure that you will die by the sword, famine, and disease in the place where you want to go and live.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking unto all the people all the words of the LORD their God, for which the LORD their God had sent him to them, even all these words,
verses.decoded: After Jeremiah finished delivering all the messages from the LORD their God to the people, the very words the LORD had sent him to speak,

verses.kjv: Then spake Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men, saying unto Jeremiah, Thou speakest falsely: the LORD our God hath not sent thee to say, Go not into Egypt to sojourn there:
verses.decoded: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the proud leaders said to Jeremiah, “You are lying; the LORD our God did not send you to tell us not to go to Egypt to live there.”

verses.kjv: But Baruch the son of Neriah setteth thee on against us, for to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us to death, and carry us away captives into Babylon.
verses.decoded: They accused Baruch son of Neriah of encouraging you to speak against us so that we would be handed over to the Babylonians, who would kill us or take us captive to Babylon.

verses.kjv: So Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, and all the people, obeyed not the voice of the LORD, to dwell in the land of Judah.
verses.decoded: So Johanan son of Kareah, the military commanders, and all the people refused to obey the LORD’s command to stay in the land of Judah.

verses.kjv: But Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces, took all the remnant of Judah, that were returned from all nations, whither they had been driven, to dwell in the land of Judah;
verses.decoded: Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and the commanders gathered all the remaining people of Judah who had returned from the nations where they had been scattered,

verses.kjv: Even men, and women, and children, and the king’s daughters, and every person that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch the son of Neriah.
verses.decoded: including men, women, children, the king’s daughters, and everyone that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left under the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam, Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch son of Neriah.

verses.kjv: So they came into the land of Egypt: for they obeyed not the voice of the LORD: thus came they even to Tahpanhes.
verses.decoded: Then they went into Egypt because they did not obey the LORD’s command; they arrived at Tahpanhes in Egypt.

verses.kjv: Then came the word of the LORD unto Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.decoded: While Jeremiah was in Tahpanhes, the LORD gave him another message, saying,

verses.kjv: Take great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln, which is at the entry of Pharaoh’s house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah;
verses.decoded: Take large stones and hide them in the clay inside the brick kiln at the entrance of Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, where the people of Judah can see you.

verses.kjv: And say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid; and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them.
verses.decoded: Tell them, ‘This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I will send Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will place his throne on the stones I have hidden. He will spread his royal canopy over them.’

verses.kjv: And when he cometh, he shall smite the land of Egypt, and deliver such as are for death to death; and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword.
verses.decoded: When he arrives, he will attack Egypt, putting those destined to die to death, those meant for captivity into captivity, and those meant for the sword to the sword.

verses.kjv: And I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt; and he shall burn them, and carry them away captives: and he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd putteth on his garment; and he shall go forth from thence in peace.
verses.decoded: I will set fire to the temples of Egypt’s gods; he will burn them and take captives. He will take control of Egypt like a shepherd putting on a cloak, then leave peacefully.

verses.kjv: He shall break also the images of Bethshemesh, that is in the land of Egypt; and the houses of the gods of the Egyptians shall he burn with fire.
verses.decoded: He will also smash the statues of Bethshemesh in Egypt and burn the temples of the Egyptian gods with fire.

verses.kjv: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews which dwell in the land of Egypt, which dwell at Migdol, and at Tahpanhes, and at Noph, and in the country of Pathros, saying,
verses.decoded: This message came to Jeremiah about all the Jews living in Egypt, in places like Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph, and the region of Pathros.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Ye have seen all the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, and upon all the cities of Judah; and, behold, this day they are a desolation, and no man dwelleth therein,
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disasters I have brought on Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah; now they are ruins, and no one lives there.

verses.kjv: Because of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to anger, in that they went to burn incense, and to serve other gods, whom they knew not, neither they, ye, nor your fathers.
verses.decoded: This happened because of their sins that made me angry—they burned incense and worshiped other gods they didn’t even know, neither they, you, nor your ancestors.

verses.kjv: Howbeit I sent unto you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, Oh, do not this abominable thing that I hate.
verses.decoded: But I sent my servants, the prophets, to you early and often, warning, 'Don’t do this disgusting thing that I hate.'

verses.kjv: But they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness, to burn no incense unto other gods.
verses.decoded: Yet they did not listen or pay attention; they refused to stop their evil ways and continued to burn incense to other gods.

verses.kjv: Wherefore my fury and mine anger was poured forth, and was kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they are wasted and desolate, as at this day.
verses.decoded: So my anger exploded in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem; now they are destroyed and empty, just as they are today.

verses.kjv: Therefore now thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; Wherefore commit ye this great evil against your souls, to cut off from you man and woman, child and suckling, out of Judah, to leave you none to remain;
verses.decoded: Now the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Why do you do this terrible harm to yourselves by killing men, women, children, and babies from Judah, leaving no one alive?

verses.kjv: In that ye provoke me unto wrath with the works of your hands, burning incense unto other gods in the land of Egypt, whither ye be gone to dwell, that ye might cut yourselves off, and that ye might be a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.decoded: You make me angry by burning incense to other gods here in Egypt, where you have gone to live. By doing this, you are destroying yourselves and becoming a curse and disgrace to all nations.

verses.kjv: Have ye forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives, which they have committed in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?
verses.decoded: Have you forgotten the sins of your ancestors, the kings of Judah, their wives, your own sins, and the sins of your wives, all committed in Judah and Jerusalem’s streets?

verses.kjv: They are not humbled even unto this day, neither have they feared, nor walked in my law, nor in my statutes, that I set before you and before your fathers.
verses.decoded: They have not been truly sorry even until now; they have not feared me or followed my laws and commands that I gave to you and your ancestors.

verses.kjv: Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, and to cut off all Judah.
verses.decoded: So the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I will turn against you to bring disaster and destroy all of Judah.

verses.kjv: And I will take the remnant of Judah, that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they shall all be consumed, and fall in the land of Egypt; they shall even be consumed by the sword and by the famine: they shall die, from the least even unto the greatest, by the sword and by the famine: and they shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach.
verses.decoded: I will destroy the remaining people of Judah who decided to go live in Egypt. They will all perish there by sword and famine, from the youngest to the oldest. They will become a horror story, a curse, and a disgrace.

verses.kjv: For I will punish them that dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence:
verses.decoded: I will punish those living in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem—with sword, famine, and disease.

verses.kjv: So that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah, to the which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none shall return but such as shall escape.
verses.decoded: None of the remaining people of Judah who went to live in Egypt will survive or stay alive to return to Judah, the land they long to go back to—only a few survivors will return.

verses.kjv: Then all the men which knew that their wives had burned incense unto other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great multitude, even all the people that dwelt in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,
verses.decoded: Then all the men who knew their wives had burned incense to other gods, along with all the women and a large crowd of people living in Egypt, in Pathros, responded to Jeremiah, saying,

verses.kjv: As for the word that thou hast spoken unto us in the name of the LORD, we will not hearken unto thee.
verses.decoded: We will not listen to the message you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD.

verses.kjv: But we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth, to burn incense unto the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, as we have done, we, and our fathers, our kings, and our princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem: for then had we plenty of victuals, and were well, and saw no evil.
verses.decoded: But we will definitely do whatever we decide ourselves: we will burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we and our ancestors, our kings, and leaders did in the cities of Judah and on the streets of Jerusalem. At that time, we had plenty of food, were prosperous, and experienced no harm.

verses.kjv: But since we left off to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword and by the famine.
verses.decoded: But since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been destroyed by war and famine.

verses.kjv: And when we burned incense to the queen of heaven, and poured out drink offerings unto her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her, without our men?
verses.decoded: When we burned incense and poured out drink offerings to the queen of heaven, did we do this without our men?

verses.kjv: Then Jeremiah said unto all the people, to the men, and to the women, and to all the people which had given him that answer, saying,
verses.decoded: Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people—men and women—who had given him that reply, saying,

verses.kjv: The incense that ye burned in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, ye, and your fathers, your kings, and your princes, and the people of the land, did not the LORD remember them, and came it not into his mind?
verses.decoded: The incense you burned in the cities of Judah and on the streets of Jerusalem—did not the LORD remember it? Did it not come to His mind?

verses.kjv: So that the LORD could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings, and because of the abominations which ye have committed; therefore is your land a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse, without an inhabitant, as at this day.
verses.decoded: The LORD could no longer tolerate your evil actions and the disgusting sins you committed. That is why your land is a wasteland, a horror, and a curse, with no people living there, just as it is today.

verses.kjv: Because ye have burned incense, and because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies; therefore this evil is happened unto you, as at this day.
verses.decoded: Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, disobeying His voice and not following His laws, rules, or commands, this disaster has come upon you, as you see today.

verses.kjv: Moreover Jeremiah said unto all the people, and to all the women, Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah that are in the land of Egypt:
verses.decoded: Jeremiah also said to all the people and women, 'Listen to the word of the LORD, all Judah living in Egypt:'

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saying; Ye and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying, We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her: ye will surely accomplish your vows, and surely perform your vows.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and acted with your hands, saying, 'We will definitely keep our promises to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' You are determined to keep your vows.

verses.kjv: Therefore hear ye the word of the LORD, all Judah that dwell in the land of Egypt; Behold, I have sworn by my great name, saith the LORD, that my name shall no more be named in the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, The Lord GOD liveth.
verses.decoded: So listen to the word of the LORD, all Judah living in Egypt: I have sworn by my great name, says the LORD, that no one from Judah in Egypt will ever again say, 'The LORD God lives.'

verses.kjv: Behold, I will watch over them for evil, and not for good: and all the men of Judah that are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by the famine, until there be an end of them.
verses.decoded: I will watch over them to bring disaster, not blessing. All the men of Judah living in Egypt will be destroyed by war and famine until they are completely gone.

verses.kjv: Yet a small number that escape the sword shall return out of the land of Egypt into the land of Judah, and all the remnant of Judah, that are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall know whose words shall stand, mine, or theirs.
verses.decoded: But a small number who survive the sword will return from Egypt to Judah. Then all the remaining people of Judah who went to live in Egypt will realize whose words are true—mine or theirs.

verses.kjv: And this shall be a sign unto you, saith the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, that ye may know that my words shall surely stand against you for evil:
verses.decoded: This will be a sign to you, says the LORD: I will punish you here so you will know that my words against you will certainly come true.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give Pharaohhophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, and into the hand of them that seek his life; as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, and that sought his life.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD says: I will hand Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, over to his enemies and those who want to kill him, just as I handed King Zedekiah of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who was his enemy and wanted to kill him.

verses.kjv: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spake unto Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, saying,
verses.decoded: This is the message that the prophet Jeremiah spoke to Baruch, son of Neriah, after Baruch had written down Jeremiah’s words in a scroll during the fourth year of King Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, unto thee, O Baruch:
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:

verses.kjv: Thou didst say, Woe is me now! for the LORD hath added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest.
verses.decoded: You said, 'Woe is me! The LORD has made my troubles even worse. I am exhausted from my deep sighing and I cannot find any peace.'

verses.kjv: Thus shalt thou say unto him, The LORD saith thus; Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up, even this whole land.
verses.decoded: Tell him this: The LORD says, 'Look, I will destroy what I have built and uproot what I have planted—all of this land.'

verses.kjv: And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the LORD: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest.
verses.decoded: Are you hoping for great things for yourself? Don’t. I will bring disaster on everyone, says the LORD. But I will protect your life and give it to you as a prize wherever you go.

verses.kjv: The word of the LORD which came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Gentiles;
verses.decoded: This is the message from the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

verses.kjv: Against Egypt, against the army of Pharaohnecho king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah.
verses.decoded: This message is against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, who was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish, where Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated them in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.

verses.kjv: Order ye the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.
verses.decoded: Get your shields and armor ready and prepare to fight.

verses.kjv: Harness the horses; and get up, ye horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, and put on the brigandines.
verses.decoded: Prepare the horses, riders, and soldiers; put on your helmets, sharpen your spears, and wear your armor.

verses.kjv: Wherefore have I seen them dismayed and turned away back? and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: for fear was round about, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: Why do I see them terrified and running away? Their strong warriors are broken and fleeing quickly without looking back, because fear surrounds them, says the LORD.

verses.kjv: Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; they shall stumble, and fall toward the north by the river Euphrates.
verses.decoded: Neither the fast nor the strong will escape; they will stumble and fall north of the Euphrates River.

verses.kjv: Who is this that cometh up as a flood, whose waters are moved as the rivers?
verses.decoded: Who is this rising like a flood, with waters flowing like rivers?

verses.kjv: Egypt riseth up like a flood, and his waters are moved like the rivers; and he saith, I will go up, and will cover the earth; I will destroy the city and the inhabitants thereof.
verses.decoded: Egypt rises like a flood, its forces moving like rivers, saying, 'I will advance and cover the land; I will destroy the city and its people.'

verses.kjv: Come up, ye horses; and rage, ye chariots; and let the mighty men come forth; the Ethiopians and the Libyans, that handle the shield; and the Lydians, that handle and bend the bow.
verses.decoded: Horses, charge! Chariots, rush forward! Let the warriors come out—the Ethiopians and Libyans who carry shields, and the Lydians who use and bend their bows.

verses.kjv: For this is the day of the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour, and it shall be satiate and made drunk with their blood: for the Lord GOD of hosts hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.
verses.decoded: This is the day of the LORD, the God of armies—a day of punishment to take revenge on his enemies. The sword will consume them, overflowing with their blood, because the LORD has a sacrifice prepared in the northern land by the Euphrates River.

verses.kjv: Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin, the daughter of Egypt: in vain shalt thou use many medicines; for thou shalt not be cured.
verses.decoded: Go to Gilead and get balm, O pure daughter of Egypt, but your many medicines will be useless; you will not be healed.

verses.kjv: The nations have heard of thy shame, and thy cry hath filled the land: for the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty, and they are fallen both together.
verses.decoded: The nations have heard of your disgrace, and your cries have spread throughout the land, because strong warriors have clashed and both have fallen.

verses.kjv: The word that the LORD spake to Jeremiah the prophet, how Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: This is the message the LORD gave to Jeremiah the prophet about how Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, would attack Egypt.

verses.kjv: Declare ye in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Noph and in Tahpanhes: say ye, Stand fast, and prepare thee; for the sword shall devour round about thee.
verses.decoded: Announce this in Egypt, in Migdol, Noph, and Tahpanhes: Prepare yourselves and stand firm, because the sword will surround you.

verses.kjv: Why are thy valiant men swept away? they stood not, because the LORD did drive them.
verses.decoded: Why have your brave men been defeated? They did not stand their ground because the LORD forced them to flee.

verses.kjv: He made many to fall, yea, one fell upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.
verses.decoded: He caused many to fall, one on top of another; and they said, 'Get up, let’s return to our own people and to our homeland, away from the attacking sword.'

verses.kjv: They did cry there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath passed the time appointed.
verses.decoded: They shouted there, 'Pharaoh king of Egypt is just empty noise; his time has run out.'

verses.kjv: As I live, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts, Surely as Tabor is among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.
verses.decoded: As surely as I live—declares the LORD of armies—he will come like Mount Tabor among the mountains and like Mount Carmel by the sea.

verses.kjv: O thou daughter dwelling in Egypt, furnish thyself to go into captivity: for Noph shall be waste and desolate without an inhabitant.
verses.decoded: O daughter living in Egypt, prepare yourself to be taken captive; for Memphis (Noph) will become a wasteland, deserted and empty.

verses.kjv: Egypt is like a very fair heifer, but destruction cometh; it cometh out of the north.
verses.decoded: Egypt is like a beautiful young cow, but destruction is coming from the north.

verses.kjv: Also her hired men are in the midst of her like fatted bullocks; for they also are turned back, and are fled away together: they did not stand, because the day of their calamity was come upon them, and the time of their visitation.
verses.decoded: Her mercenaries inside her are like well-fed bulls, but they have turned and fled together; they did not hold their ground because their day of disaster and punishment had arrived.

verses.kjv: The voice thereof shall go like a serpent; for they shall march with an army, and come against her with axes, as hewers of wood.
verses.decoded: Their attack will be like the hiss of a snake; they will march as an army and come against her with axes, like woodcutters.

verses.kjv: They shall cut down her forest, saith the LORD, though it cannot be searched; because they are more than the grasshoppers, and are innumerable.
verses.decoded: They will destroy her forests—declares the LORD—even though they cannot be fully counted, because they are more numerous than grasshoppers.

verses.kjv: The daughter of Egypt shall be confounded; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.
verses.decoded: The daughter of Egypt will be ashamed and handed over to the people from the north.

verses.kjv: The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, saith; Behold, I will punish the multitude of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with their gods, and their kings; even Pharaoh, and all them that trust in him:
verses.decoded: The LORD of armies, the God of Israel, says: I will punish the people of No (Thebes), Pharaoh, Egypt, their gods, and their kings—Pharaoh and all who trust in him.

verses.kjv: And I will deliver them into the hand of those that seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants: and afterward it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: I will hand them over to those who want to kill them, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants; later, the land will be inhabited again as in former times—declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
verses.decoded: But do not be afraid, my servant Jacob; do not be discouraged, Israel. I will save you from far away and your descendants from exile. Jacob will come back and live in peace and safety, with no one to frighten him.

verses.kjv: Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the LORD: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.
verses.decoded: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant—declares the LORD—for I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I scattered you, but I will not destroy you completely. I will discipline you fairly but will not leave you without any punishment.

verses.kjv: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.
verses.decoded: This is the message from the LORD given to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines, before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD; Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall be an overflowing flood, and shall overflow the land, and all that is therein; the city, and them that dwell therein: then the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl.
verses.decoded: The LORD says: Look, waters are coming from the north like a flood that will overflow the land, the city, and everyone living there. People will cry out and all the inhabitants will wail.

verses.kjv: At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong horses, at the rushing of his chariots, and at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers shall not look back to their children for feebleness of hands;
verses.decoded: When you hear the loud stamping of his powerful horses, the rushing of his chariots, and the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers will be too weak to look back at their children.

verses.kjv: Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.
verses.decoded: Because a day is coming to destroy all the Philistines and to cut off every ally left from Tyre and Sidon. The LORD will destroy the Philistines, the survivors from the island of Caphtor.

verses.kjv: Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?
verses.decoded: Gaza has been struck down and is like a bald head; Ashkelon is destroyed along with the survivors in its valley. How long will you continue to mourn and injure yourself?

verses.kjv: O thou sword of the LORD, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still.
verses.decoded: O sword of the LORD, how long will you remain active? Sheathe yourself, rest, and be still.

verses.kjv: How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it.
verses.decoded: How can the sword rest when the LORD has commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the coastal region? That is where He has sent it.

verses.kjv: Against Moab thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Woe unto Nebo! for it is spoiled: Kiriathaim is confounded and taken: Misgab is confounded and dismayed.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says against Moab: "Woe to Nebo! It has been destroyed. Kiriathaim is confused and captured. Misgab is shaken and terrified."

verses.kjv: There shall be no more praise of Moab: in Heshbon they have devised evil against it; come, and let us cut it off from being a nation. Also thou shalt be cut down, O Madmen; the sword shall pursue thee.
verses.decoded: Moab will no longer be praised. In Heshbon, enemies have planned evil against it, saying, "Let’s wipe it out as a nation." You will be silenced, Moab, and the sword will chase you down.

verses.kjv: A voice of crying shall be from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction.
verses.decoded: From Horonaim comes a loud cry of ruin and severe destruction.

verses.kjv: Moab is destroyed; her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
verses.decoded: Moab is ruined; even the children’s cries are heard in the distress.

verses.kjv: For in the going up of Luhith continual weeping shall go up; for in the going down of Horonaim the enemies have heard a cry of destruction.
verses.decoded: As people climb up from Luhith, constant weeping rises; as they descend from Horonaim, enemies hear the sounds of destruction.

verses.kjv: Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness.
verses.decoded: Run for your lives and be like a bush in the desert—bare and exposed.

verses.kjv: For because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together.
verses.decoded: Because you trusted in your own achievements and wealth, you will be captured. Even Chemosh, your god, will be taken into exile along with his priests and leaders.

verses.kjv: And the spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape: the valley also shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed, as the LORD hath spoken.
verses.decoded: The destroyer will attack every city; none will be spared. The valleys and plains will be ruined, just as the LORD has declared.

verses.kjv: Give wings unto Moab, that it may flee and get away: for the cities thereof shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein.
verses.decoded: Let Moab fly away like a bird to escape, because its cities will be empty and abandoned.

verses.kjv: Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.
verses.decoded: Cursed is anyone who does the LORD’s work carelessly or dishonestly, and cursed is anyone who refuses to use their sword to bring judgment.

verses.kjv: Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed.
verses.decoded: Moab has lived comfortably from youth, like wine left undisturbed on its sediment, never transferred or taken captive; so its character and pride have stayed the same.

verses.kjv: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will send unto him wanderers, that shall cause him to wander, and shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles.
verses.decoded: But now, the LORD says, the time is coming when I will send raiders who will make Moab wander like lost travelers, emptying their resources and breaking their containers.

verses.kjv: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence.
verses.decoded: Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as Israel was ashamed of Bethel, the place they trusted in.

verses.kjv: How say ye, We are mighty and strong men for the war?
verses.decoded: How can you say, 'We are mighty and strong warriors'?

verses.kjv: Moab is spoiled, and gone up out of her cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
verses.decoded: Moab has been destroyed and abandoned its cities; its best young men have been killed, says the LORD Almighty.

verses.kjv: The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast.
verses.decoded: Disaster is about to strike Moab, and its suffering is coming quickly.

verses.kjv: All ye that are about him, bemoan him; and all ye that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!
verses.decoded: Everyone around Moab, mourn for it; and all who know Moab, say, 'How has the strong support been broken, the beautiful rod snapped!'

verses.kjv: Thou daughter that dost inhabit Dibon, come down from thy glory, and sit in thirst; for the spoiler of Moab shall come upon thee, and he shall destroy thy strong holds.
verses.decoded: You, daughter of Dibon, come down from your proud position and suffer; the destroyer of Moab is coming to attack you and will ruin your fortresses.

verses.kjv: O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done?
verses.decoded: You who live in Aroer, stand by the road and watch; question those who are fleeing and those who have escaped, and ask, 'What has happened?'

verses.kjv: Moab is confounded; for it is broken down: howl and cry; tell ye it in Arnon, that Moab is spoiled,
verses.decoded: Moab is shattered and destroyed; cry out in grief and announce at Arnon that Moab has been ruined.

verses.kjv: And judgment is come upon the plain country; upon Holon, and upon Jahazah, and upon Mephaath,
verses.decoded: Judgment has come on the plains, including Holon, Jahazah, and Mephaath.

verses.kjv: And upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Bethdiblathaim,
verses.decoded: Also upon Dibon, Nebo, and Bethdiblathaim.

verses.kjv: And upon Kiriathaim, and upon Bethgamul, and upon Bethmeon,
verses.decoded: And upon Kiriathaim, Bethgamul, and Bethmeon.

verses.kjv: And upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
verses.decoded: And upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the cities of Moab, whether near or far.

verses.kjv: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: The power of Moab is destroyed, and its strength is broken, declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: Make ye him drunken: for he magnified himself against the LORD: Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
verses.decoded: Make Moab drunk with shame because it has exalted itself against the LORD; Moab will be humiliated and mocked.

verses.kjv: For was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy.
verses.decoded: Was Israel not a joke to you? Was Israel ever caught stealing? Yet when you talked about Israel, you rejoiced with pride.

verses.kjv: O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole’s mouth.
verses.decoded: People of Moab, abandon your cities and live in the cliffs, like a dove nesting in the rocky caves.

verses.kjv: We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
verses.decoded: We have heard about Moab’s great pride, arrogance, and the haughtiness of its heart.

verses.kjv: I know his wrath, saith the LORD; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.
verses.decoded: I am aware of Moab’s anger, says the LORD, but it will not succeed; its falsehoods will not prevail.

verses.kjv: Therefore will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; mine heart shall mourn for the men of Kirheres.
verses.decoded: That is why I will wail for Moab and cry out for all of Moab; my heart will grieve for the people of Kirheres.

verses.kjv: O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for thee with the weeping of Jazer: thy plants are gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage.
verses.decoded: O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for you as deeply as I wept for Jazer. Your vines have spread across the sea, reaching even to the Sea of Jazer. But destruction has come upon your summer crops and your harvest.

verses.kjv: And joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; their shouting shall be no shouting.
verses.decoded: Joy and happiness have disappeared from the fertile fields and from the land of Moab. I have stopped the wine from flowing in the winepresses; no one will stomp the grapes with joyful shouts—their shouting will be silent.

verses.kjv: From the cry of Heshbon even unto Elealeh, and even unto Jahaz, have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even unto Horonaim, as an heifer of three years old: for the waters also of Nimrim shall be desolate.
verses.decoded: From the cries of Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, voices are raised; from Zoar to Horonaim, they sound like a young three-year-old heifer. Even the waters of Nimrim will dry up and become desolate.

verses.kjv: Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, saith the LORD, him that offereth in the high places, and him that burneth incense to his gods.
verses.decoded: Furthermore, I will stop all those in Moab who offer sacrifices on the high places and burn incense to their gods, declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: Therefore mine heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and mine heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kirheres: because the riches that he hath gotten are perished.
verses.decoded: So my heart will mourn for Moab like the sound of pipes; it will mourn like pipes for the people of Kirheres, because the wealth they had is gone.

verses.kjv: For every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: upon all the hands shall be cuttings, and upon the loins sackcloth.
verses.decoded: Everyone will have shaved heads and trimmed beards; all will wear marks of mourning on their hands and sackcloth around their waists.

verses.kjv: There shall be lamentation generally upon all the housetops of Moab, and in the streets thereof: for I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein is no pleasure, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: There will be widespread mourning on every rooftop and in the streets of Moab, because I have shattered Moab like a broken jar that is no longer useful, declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: They shall howl, saying, How is it broken down! how hath Moab turned the back with shame! so shall Moab be a derision and a dismaying to all them about him.
verses.decoded: They will wail, saying, 'How has it fallen! How has Moab turned away in shame!' Moab will become a joke and a horror to all its neighbors.

verses.kjv: For thus saith the LORD; Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD says: Look, someone will swoop down like an eagle and spread their wings over Moab.

verses.kjv: Kerioth is taken, and the strong holds are surprised, and the mighty men’s hearts in Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
verses.decoded: Kerioth is captured, and the fortresses are taken by surprise. On that day, the brave men of Moab will be terrified, trembling like a woman in labor.

verses.kjv: And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the LORD.
verses.decoded: Moab will be wiped out as a nation because it has exalted itself against the LORD.

verses.kjv: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: Fear, traps, and pitfalls will come upon you, people of Moab, declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: Anyone who tries to escape fear will fall into a pit; anyone who climbs out of the pit will be caught in a trap. I will bring judgment on Moab in their appointed time, declares the LORD.

verses.kjv: They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
verses.decoded: Those who fled took shelter near Heshbon because of the attacking army, but fire will burst out from Heshbon and flames from the heart of Sihon, consuming the outskirts of Moab and the leaders of the noisy rebels.

verses.kjv: Woe be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth: for thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.
verses.decoded: Trouble is coming to you, Moab! The people who worship Chemosh will be destroyed because your sons and daughters have been taken as prisoners.

verses.kjv: Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the LORD. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
verses.decoded: But in the future, I will restore Moab and bring back those who were taken captive, says the LORD. This is the extent of Moab's punishment.

verses.kjv: Concerning the Ammonites, thus saith the LORD; Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?
verses.decoded: This message is about the Ammonites. The LORD says: Doesn’t Israel have any sons or heirs? Then why does their king control Gad, and why do his people live in those cities?

verses.kjv: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: So, the LORD says, the time is coming when I will send a warning of war to Rabbah, the Ammonite city. It will become a ruined wasteland, and its towns will be burned. Then Israel will take back the land that once belonged to them.

verses.kjv: Howl, O Heshbon, for Ai is spoiled: cry, ye daughters of Rabbah, gird you with sackcloth; lament, and run to and fro by the hedges; for their king shall go into captivity, and his priests and his princes together.
verses.decoded: Cry out, Heshbon, because Ai has been destroyed. Women of Rabbah, put on sackcloth to mourn; lament and wander near the city walls. Their king, along with his priests and leaders, will be taken captive.

verses.kjv: Wherefore gloriest thou in the valleys, thy flowing valley, O backsliding daughter? that trusted in her treasures, saying, Who shall come unto me?
verses.decoded: Why do you boast about your fertile valleys, you unfaithful daughter, who trusted in your wealth and said, ‘Who can attack me?’

verses.kjv: Behold, I will bring a fear upon thee, saith the Lord GOD of hosts, from all those that be about thee; and ye shall be driven out every man right forth; and none shall gather up him that wandereth.
verses.decoded: The LORD of heavenly armies says: I will cause fear to come upon you from all around. Everyone will be forced to flee quickly, and no one will help those who get lost or stray.

verses.kjv: And afterward I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: Later, I will restore the Ammonite people from captivity, says the LORD.

verses.kjv: Concerning Edom, thus saith the LORD of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?
verses.decoded: About Edom, the LORD of heavenly armies says: Has wisdom disappeared from Teman? Has good advice vanished from the wise? Has their understanding been lost?

verses.kjv: Flee ye, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time that I will visit him.
verses.decoded: Run away, turn back, and hide deep underground, people of Dedan, because I will bring disaster on Esau’s descendants when I come to punish them.

verses.kjv: If grapegatherers come to thee, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? if thieves by night, they will destroy till they have enough.
verses.decoded: If grape pickers come to you, wouldn’t they leave some grapes behind? But if thieves come at night, they will steal everything until they have taken enough.

verses.kjv: But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled, and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he is not.
verses.decoded: But I have exposed Esau’s secrets and uncovered his hiding places. He will not be able to hide. His descendants, relatives, and neighbors have been destroyed, and he no longer exists.

verses.kjv: Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.
verses.decoded: Leave your fatherless children behind; I will protect them. Let your widows put their hope in me.

verses.kjv: For thus saith the LORD; Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken; and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it.
verses.decoded: The LORD says: Those who were not supposed to suffer judgment have already suffered it. Do you think you will escape punishment? You will not; you will certainly face it.

verses.kjv: For I have sworn by myself, saith the LORD, that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.
verses.decoded: I have sworn by myself, says the LORD, that Bozrah will become a ruined, shameful wasteland, cursed forever. All its cities will remain deserted forever.

verses.kjv: I have heard a rumour from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent unto the heathen, saying, Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.
verses.decoded: I have heard a message from the LORD: a messenger has been sent to the nations, saying, ‘Gather your armies and come to fight against her; prepare for battle.’

verses.kjv: For, lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men.
verses.decoded: I will make you insignificant among the nations and hated by all people.

verses.kjv: Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the LORD.
verses.decoded: Your power has fooled you, and your pride has misled you, you who live in the rocky cliffs and hold the high hills. Even if you build your nest as high as an eagle's, I will bring you down from there, says the LORD.

verses.kjv: Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.
verses.decoded: Edom will become a wasteland; everyone who passes by will be shocked and will mock the disasters that have come upon it.

verses.kjv: As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the LORD, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.
